text: As the Patriots prep for Sunday's 1 PM ET showdown against the Jaguars in Jacksonville, the storylines are predictably mixed—rookie linebacker Gabe Jacas continues his promising start as a second-round pick after making impact plays in the first two weeks, while tight end Eli Raridon's return to practice offers some positive news despite his thigh injury leaving him questionable for the contest (safety Craig Woodson remains questionable with a shoulder issue, though both made the trip). The Patriots have elevated safety Mike Brown and defensive tackle Jeremiah Pharms Jr. to the active roster, addressing some depth concerns as Jacksonville's defense looks to deploy Cover-6 coverage extensively, a scheme the Patriots will need to scheme against with timing-based "X" plays. Beyond the chess match up front, there's been some self-awareness emerging from the team about their clock management in the final moments before halftime over the last two weeks—a fixable problem that could prove costly against a Jaguars offense looking to bounce back from their worst performance in eleven months with Trevor Lawrence leading the charge.
